title: How Classical Infrastructure Enables Quantum Computing and AI
excerpt: Servers, GPUs, storage and networking give agencies a foundation for AI deployment, quantum experimentation and the transition to post-quantum security.
content:
Oct 30 2026

Artificial Intelligence

Servers, GPUs, storage and networking give agencies a foundation for AI deployment, quantum experimentation and the transition to post-quantum security.

Nathan Eddy works as an independent filmmaker and journalist based in Berlin, specializing in architecture, business technology and healthcare IT. He is a graduate of Northwestern University’s Medill School of Journalism. 

Federal agencies exploring quantum computing still need familiar infrastructure: servers, accelerators, storage and high-speed networks. Those systems run artificial intelligence applications while supporting the simulations and control functions needed to develop quantum capabilities.a

For technology leaders, that overlap creates an opportunity to build infrastructure around several needs, even as quantum applications mature at different speeds.

Ken Rollins, federal field CTO for emerging technologies at Dell Federal, describes the relationship between AI and quantum computing as “bidirectional,” with AI helping improve quantum systems today and quantum computing potentially accelerating AI in the future.

“There’s a lot going on right now with AI enabling quantum,” he says.

Understanding that distinction can help agencies separate practical investments from longer-term experimentation while preparing for the security changes quantum computing will require.
